issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court may interfere with concurrent convictions when material evidence has been misread or overlooked and the resulting findings are perverse or cause a miscarriage of justice.
material_facts: The appeal challenged convictions affirmed by the High Court.

The prosecution witnesses gave materially inconsistent accounts of who inflicted the fatal injury, and the courts below had treated their accounts as corroborative without addressing those inconsistencies.
The Supreme Court reappreciated the evidence and found that the convictions had been recorded while overlooking material contradictions.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court was entitled to reappraise the evidence, set aside the concurrent convictions, and acquit the appellants.
issues.legal_principle: Section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure concerns appeals from convictions. Although the Supreme Court ordinarily does not reassess evidence merely to reach a fresh view on guilt, it may interfere where evidence has been improperly received or rejected, vital evidence has been misread, or important points favouring the accused have been overlooked; see Saravanabhavan v. State of Madras. Where a High Court's factual finding is perverse and has caused a miscarriage of justice, the Supreme Court may hear the appeal on the evidence; see Kashmira Singh v. State of Madhya Pradesh. Under Article 136 of the Constitution, concurrent findings may be disturbed when perverse, and the Supreme Court may reappreciate evidence where the courts below have failed to assess it properly; see Ashoksinh Jayendrasinh v. State of Gujarat and Mahesh Dattatray Thirthkar v. State of Maharashtra.

rule.if: appeal_against_conviction and concurrent_conviction_findings and material_evidence_overlooked and resulting_findings_perverse

predicates.appeal_against_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a conviction.
predicates.concurrent_conviction_findings: The trial court convicted the accused and the appellate court affirmed that conviction.
predicates.material_evidence_overlooked: The courts below failed to take account of significant evidence or contradictions bearing on the accused's guilt.
predicates.resulting_findings_perverse: The findings of guilt are unreasonable in light of the evidence that was overlooked or misread.

issues.definition: When a conviction affirmed on appeal rests on perverse findings produced by overlooking material evidence, the conviction is set aside and the accused are acquitted.

issues.legal_issue: Related witnesses may be relied upon, but their evidence must be scrutinized with care, and material contradictions that undermine its credibility may prevent proof of guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
material_facts: The prosecution witnesses were related to the deceased and to one another.
The witnesses gave conflicting accounts of who inflicted the fatal injury, and one witness's account included a material improvement not previously reported to the police.
The evidence of the witnesses who arrived after the incident was hearsay or did not identify who inflicted the fatal injury.
The prosecution examined no independent witness, and the medical evidence established the fatal injury but did not resolve the conflicting accounts of the assailant.
issues.conclusion: The material contradictions made the prosecution evidence unreliable and insufficient to prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt; the appellants were acquitted of all charges.
issues.legal_principle: Related or interested witnesses are not to be rejected solely because of their relationship or interest, but their evidence must be examined with discerning scrutiny and care. This is a rule of prudence, not a rule of law; evidence that has a ring of truth may be relied upon even without corroboration. See Gangadhar Behera v. State of Orissa; Raju alias Balachandran v. State of Tamil Nadu, which relies on Dalip Singh v. State of Punjab and Sarwan Singh v. State of Punjab; and Ganapathi v. State of Tamil Nadu. Under State of Rajasthan v. Kalki, ordinary discrepancies do not necessarily undermine a case, while material discrepancies corrode its credibility. Here, the contradictions about who inflicted the fatal injury were material and the prosecution evidence did not establish guilt beyond reasonable doubt.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_conviction and prosecution_witnesses_related and material_contradictions_on_fatal_assault and no_independent_witnesses and guilt_not_proved_beyond_reasonable_doubt

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging a conviction.
predicates.prosecution_witnesses_related: The prosecution witnesses whose testimony supports the charge are related to one another or to the victim.
predicates.material_contradictions_on_fatal_assault: The witnesses give materially conflicting accounts about who inflicted the fatal injury.
predicates.no_independent_witnesses: The prosecution presents no independent witness to support its account of the incident.
predicates.guilt_not_proved_beyond_reasonable_doubt: The evidence, considered as a whole, does not establish the accused's guilt beyond reasonable doubt.

issues.definition: When related prosecution witnesses give materially conflicting accounts of the fatal assault, no independent witness supports the prosecution, and the evidence does not prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt, the accused are acquitted of all charges.
